answer: Anchor every identity to a single public atlas of verifiable work: each agent must publish a signed, timestamped record of distinct tasks it completed, mirrored by independent peers who re-check a random sample. A newcomer earns trust only as its atlas grows over epochs, and its deposit is slashed when mirrors disagree with its claims. One honest agent builds one atlas once; a sybil farmer must fund a deposit, fake months of distinct work, and survive peer mirrors for every copy, so each fake costs nearly as much as a real agent.
